title: Deleting a running job leaves an uncancellable fleet execution, recreates orphaned history, and can resurrect the job in jobs.json
existing_state: UpdateJobActionState keeps Delete enabled while a job is running (JobListDialog.cs:896, 902 — only Run Now/Cancel are gated on isRunning). DeleteSelectedJob (JobListDialog.cs:1369-1385) confirms with just "Delete job 'X'?" then removes the job and all history without checking IsJobRunning or calling CancelJob. Three concrete consequences: (1) the in-flight SSH execution keeps running against every target host, and since the grid row is gone there is no remaining UI surface to cancel it (JobExecutionService.CancelJob needs the jobId from a row, Services/JobExecutionService.cs:274-282) — it runs to completion no matter what. (2) When it finishes, JobHistoryService's JobCompleted subscription (Services/JobHistoryService.cs:36-47) writes the run payload, recreating job-history/<deleted-id>/ immediately after DeleteAllHistory wiped it — an orphan directory nothing can ever clean up because the only delete path requires the job row. (3) For One-Time jobs, HandlePostExecution holds the captured JobDefinition reference and calls _jobStorage.Save(job) on success or scheduled failure (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:875-888); Save unconditionally re-inserts it (_jobs[job.Id] = job, JobStorageService.cs:135) — the deleted job literally reappears in jobs.json complete with hosts and credentials.
recommendation: In DeleteSelectedJob, check _executionService.IsJobRunning first: either block with "Cancel the running job before deleting" or offer "Cancel and delete" (call CancelJob, then delete). In JobExecutionService, make the post-run writers tolerant of deletion: HandlePostExecution should re-fetch via _jobStorage.Get(job.Id) and skip Save when null (CompleteJob at lines 827-832 already does exactly this), and JobHistoryService.OnJobCompleted could accept a job-exists predicate to skip writing history for deleted ids.
user_benefit: Deleting a job actually stops it; no zombie SSH runs against the fleet, no undeleteable history directories, and no one-time jobs rising from the dead in jobs.json.
mockup_idea: Before/after of the delete confirmation: current generic "Delete job 'X'?" vs a running-aware dialog showing a live-run warning with [Cancel run and delete] / [Keep job] buttons.

evidence.note: Delete enabled while running; no IsJobRunning check or CancelJob before delete
HandlePostExecution saves the captured job object back (resurrection); CompleteJob shows the correct Get-then-skip pattern; CancelJob requires the jobId
JobCompleted subscription writes run history unconditionally, recreating the deleted job's history dir
Save unconditionally re-inserts _jobs[job.Id] = job and persists
